hypothesis: Question: does the development leader (idea-a0bc19, Poisson HGB all features, dev RMSE 54.009) leave recoverable error from (a) year-by-month interactions that cannot transfer to unseen (yr=1, mnth) combinations and (b) single-model variance, such that averaging comparable HGB variants or dropping mnth/season improves later-period transfer? Recorded evidence: a0bc19 internal folds gave poisson_all 60.80 vs squared_all 60.96 mean RMSE with opposite-signed biases in cut_396/cut_456, suggesting partially complementary errors; poisson_no_elapsed was worse (63.53), so elapsed_day is kept. idea-cf138a showed recency weighting did not help (hl_none selected in all 3 folds, identical submission to a0bc19, dev RMSE 54.009), which moved my view away from time-weighting and toward representation/ensemble questions. The cut_425 fold (train through mid-March 2012, holdout Mar-Apr 2012) had bias -104 for every candidate, indicating the spring level shift is the dominant untransferred component and is unlikely to be fixed by these variants; this test is therefore bounded. Contrasting expected outcomes: (1) avg_poisson_all_squared or avg_all_three wins internal folds by 1-3% mean RMSE and submits a slightly lower dev RMSE (<54.0); (2) poisson_no_month_season wins if month effects are mostly weather proxies whose year-interaction fails to transfer; (3) poisson_all wins all folds, in which case the program submits exactly the a0bc19 predictor (ties favor it) and the informative result is that feature-subset/loss averaging does not help, leaving a0bc19 as the fixed selection. Only sample-independent model variants of the same hyperparameters vary; the selection is by mean RMSE over 3 chronological 61-day folds as in cf138a. Fallbacks are reported explicitly. Unverified: whether development gains would transfer to Jul-Dec 2012 where yr=1 and mnth>=7 are jointly unseen.
